title: Core: Zoom tool refinements - Hide reset button when value is initial

## What I did

<!-- Briefly describe what your PR does -->
The reset button is no longer displayed when Zoom is in its initial state.
I used `visibility: hidden` to ensure the menu width remains consistent even when the button is hidden.
Since the styling isn't complex and many parts already use inline styles, I added them inline to make it easier to see which styles apply under which conditions.

**Width shifts when reset button unmounts due to lack of space reservation.**

The `NumericInput` component only applies `paddingRight: 2` and renders the `after` slot when `after` is truthy (lines 57, 189 in NumericInput.tsx). When zoom is at 100%, the reset button is removed entirely, eliminating both the padding and the button's width, causing the input to shift. Consider wrapping the `after` content with a fixed-width container or always rendering an empty placeholder to maintain consistent layout.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/core/src/manager/components/preview/tools/zoom.tsx` around lines 84 -
93, The input shifts because NumericInput only renders the after slot when
truthy; when value === INITIAL_ZOOM_LEVEL the ActionList.Button (reset) unmounts
and its paddingRight is removed. Fix by always rendering the after slot as a
fixed-width container (or an empty placeholder) inside NumericInput’s after prop
so the space is reserved even when INITIAL_ZOOM_LEVEL hides the
ActionList.Button; update the zoom control (the conditional around
ActionList.Button that uses INITIAL_ZOOM_LEVEL and zoomTo) to render a
placeholder element of equal width instead of null.
```

</details>

<!-- fingerprinting:phantom:poseidon:eagle -->

comments.label_reasoning: The layout shifts when the reset button unmounts because the padding reservation is lost — this is a missing edge case / incorrect conditional rendering causing a visual bug.

# Run the verification script from the comment to check for global [hidden] rules
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== 1) Searching for global [hidden] CSS rules ==="
rg -n --type=css --type=scss --type=less '\[hidden\]' 2>/dev/null || echo "No [hidden] in CSS/SCSS/LESS files"

echo
echo "=== 2) Searching in JS/TS/JSX files for [hidden] or display:none related rules ==="
rg -n '\[hidden\]|display.*none' code/core/src --type=ts --type=tsx --type=js --type=jsx 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo "No matches found"

echo
echo "=== 3) Checking for global stylesheets or reset styles ==="
fd -t f '\.(css|scss|less)$' code/core/src | xargs rg -l 'reset|normalize|\[hidden\]' 2>/dev/null || echo "No global reset files with [hidden] found"

echo
echo "=== 4) Confirming current Button forwarding path ==="
rg -n -C5 'shouldForwardProp|hidden=\{hidden\}|visibility.*hidden' code/core/src/components/components/Button/Button.tsx 2>/dev/null || echo "Pattern not found"
```

Length of output: 1526

fd -t f -e stories.tsx -e test.tsx code/core/src/components/components/Button/ | xargs grep -l 'hidden' 2>/dev/null || echo "No hidden references in Button stories/tests"
```

Repository: storybookjs/storybook

Length of output: 604

---



</details>

**Avoid forwarding `hidden` to the DOM; use a transient prop to clarify styling-only intent.**

Line 143 forwards `hidden` to the underlying element while Line 224 also applies CSS `visibility`. This creates semantic confusion—the `hidden` attribute signifies an element is not relevant, while `visibility:hidden` preserves layout space. Using a transient prop (e.g., `$hidden`) would prevent unintended DOM forwarding and make the styling-only intent explicit.



<details>
<summary>Proposed refactor (use non-forwarded transient prop)</summary>

```diff
-            hidden={hidden}
+            $hidden={hidden}
```

In `StyledButton` props definition:
```diff
-  hidden?: boolean;
+  $hidden?: boolean;
```

In `StyledButton` style function and `shouldForwardProp`:
```diff
-  shouldForwardProp: (prop) => isPropValid(prop),
+  shouldForwardProp: (prop) => isPropValid(prop) && prop !== '$hidden',
```

```diff
-    visibility: hidden ? 'hidden' : 'visible',
+    visibility: $hidden ? 'hidden' : 'visible',
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/components/components/Button/Button.tsx` around lines 142 -
143, The Button component is forwarding the semantic HTML hidden attribute to
the DOM; change the styling-only prop to a transient prop (rename hidden →
$hidden) so it won't be forwarded. Update the StyledButton props/interface to
use $hidden, update its style logic (visibility rules that referenced hidden) to
use $hidden, add a shouldForwardProp (or rely on transient prop behavior) to
prevent forwarding, and update the Button JSX where you pass hidden to instead
pass $hidden while keeping the public API for consumers (e.g., keep the Button
prop named hidden and map it internally to $hidden when rendering StyledButton).
```

</details>

comments.author: superLipbalm
comments.body:
@Sidnioulz 
I hadn't been using the HTML `hidden` attribute much, so I forgot about it... My apologies.
As you mentioned, modifying the shared component would have a significant impact and isn't a good idea.
I've changed it to use Emotion styled as you suggested.
However, the HTML `hidden` attribute completely removes the element from the DOM by applying `display: none`,
which differs from our intended actual behavior (`visibility: hidden`). Therefore, as CodeRabbit commented, I've opted to use only the Emotion prop and add `aria-hidden` for accessibility. Is that OK?
(I'm truly sorry for bothering you so many times.)

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests a specific code change: use Emotion styled with a transient prop ($isInitialValue) for CSS visibility instead of inline styles, and provides exact code examples for the implementation.
